headline: Solar leads in Ghaziabad: which channels to use and what they really cost
card_text: A channel-by-channel guide for Ghaziabad installers: Meta, Google Search, Maps, marketplaces and referrals, what pushes cost per lead up or down, and how to split a monthly budget.
intro:
Most Ghaziabad installers don't have a lead shortage problem. They have a lead mix problem. Solar leads in Ghaziabad arrive from Facebook forms, Google calls, Maps, IndiaMART-style marketplaces, the PM Surya Ghar portal and word of mouth, and each source brings a very different kind of buyer at a very different cost. Treat them all as one number and you end up paying for the wrong ones.

This guide compares the main channels for rooftop solar leads in Ghaziabad, explains what pushes cost per lead up or down here, and shows how to split a monthly budget so the leads turn into site surveys. If you want the locality-by-locality view of the city, read our solar marketing plan for Ghaziabad first; this post is about the channels and the money.

sections.h2: Where solar leads in Ghaziabad actually come from
sections.html:
Search for solar in Ghaziabad and the first page is full of national installer brands, directories and marketplaces: SolarSquare city pages, Loom Solar's installer lists, Sulekha and IndiaMART listings. A local installer competes with all of them for the same homeowner. In practice your enquiries will come from six places:

ChannelBuyer intentLead volumeTypical problem
Meta lead ads (Facebook, Instagram)Low to medium: they were interested, not searchingHighTenants, flat owners and people outside your area
Google Search adsHigh: they typed the needMediumClicks from Delhi and Noida if location settings are loose
Google Business Profile and MapsHighLow to medium, grows over timeSlow to build; depends on reviews
Marketplaces and directories (IndiaMART, Sulekha, Justdial)MixedMediumThe same enquiry is often shared with several sellers
PM Surya Ghar portal vendor selectionHigh, already appliedLow and unpredictableYou can't control when or whether you're picked
Referrals and society word of mouthVery highLowOnly comes once you have installations to show

None of these is the right answer alone. A steady Ghaziabad pipeline usually needs one high-volume channel, one high-intent channel and a proof engine that makes both of them cheaper.

sections.h2: What pushes cost per lead up or down in Ghaziabad
sections.html:
Two installers in the same city can see very different costs for the same channel. These are the factors that move it most here:

  1. How tight your targeting is. Ghaziabad shares borders with East Delhi and Noida. A radius drawn around Indirapuram will catch Mayur Vihar and Noida sectors too. Those leads look cheap but follow different subsidy and DISCOM rules, and many fall outside your install area.
  2. The share of high-rise housing you target. Raj Nagar Extension, Crossings Republik and parts of Indirapuram are mostly apartments. Individual flat owners rarely have roof rights, so ads aimed there produce plenty of form fills and few installable leads. Older colonies such as Kavi Nagar, Raj Nagar and Shastri Nagar have more independent houses, so fewer leads go further.
  3. Form friction. A form with no questions gives you the cheapest leads and the worst calls. Adding ownership, house type and monthly bill raises cost per lead and usually lowers cost per site visit.
  4. Season. Enquiries rise when summer bills arrive and cool off in winter. Budgets that stay flat all year pay more per lead in the slow months.
  5. Proof. An installer with recent Google reviews and real Ghaziabad rooftop photos converts more of the same clicks, which brings the cost down on every paid channel.

For reference, our own rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well. That's our result, not a market rate, and yours will depend on your targeting, offer and follow-up.

sections.h2: Paid channels: Meta for volume, Google for intent
sections.html:
Meta lead ads are usually the fastest way to get enquiries from Ghaziabad homeowners. Use pincodes or tight radiuses around the colonies your team can reach in a day, keep Ghaziabad in its own campaign, and ask three qualifying questions in the form: do you own the house, what type of house is it, and what is your average monthly bill. Our step-by-step guide to Facebook ads for solar installers covers the full setup.

Google Search ads bring fewer leads with stronger intent. Build ad groups around searches like "solar panel installation Ghaziabad", "rooftop solar Indirapuram" and "solar subsidy UP", add negative keywords such as "jobs", "franchise" and "free solar panel", and check the location report every week for clicks from outside your area. Call extensions matter here because many searchers would rather phone than fill a form.

Run both for at least a few weeks before judging them, and compare them on cost per site visit, not cost per lead. A Meta lead that costs less but never books a survey is the more expensive lead.

sections.h2: Organic and earned channels that make paid leads cheaper
sections.html:
• Google Business Profile. Set service areas for the Ghaziabad localities you cover, pick accurate categories, and post real installation photos. Maps calls cost nothing per click and come from people already looking for an installer.
  • Reviews that name the area. Ask every customer for a review after commissioning and a mention of their locality. Our system for getting more Google reviews works well for solar.
  • The PM Surya Ghar portal. Homeowners who apply on the national portal can choose from registered vendors for their DISCOM, which for Ghaziabad is PVVNL. Being registered and keeping your profile accurate is worth doing, but treat it as a bonus channel: you can't advertise inside it or predict the volume.
  • Referrals. A small referral thank-you for installed customers, plus a WhatsApp message with your number after the system goes live, turns a few installations into a reliable trickle of the warmest leads you'll get.

sections.h2: Buying marketplace leads: when it makes sense
sections.html:
Marketplaces and directories are attractive because they need no setup. Before you pay for a plan, check three things:

  1. Exclusivity. Ask whether each enquiry goes to you alone or to several sellers. Shared leads go to whoever calls first and quotes lowest.
  2. Location filtering. Make sure you only receive Ghaziabad (or your chosen localities) and only rooftop solar, not solar lights, inverters or generic electrical work.
  3. Contract length. Start with the shortest plan available and track every lead in the same sheet as your own campaigns.

Marketplace leads can fill gaps, but they build nothing you own. Your Google profile, reviews and ad accounts keep working for you long after a subscription ends.

sections.h2: Get the local facts right on every call
sections.html:
A Ghaziabad lead can be lost on the first call if your team quotes Delhi's rules. Keep these straight:

  • DISCOM: Ghaziabad is served by Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited (PVVNL), so net-metering and load enhancement go through PVVNL and UPPCL's process.
  • Central subsidy: under PM Surya Ghar, eligible homes can get central assistance of up to ₹78,000 for systems of 3 kW and above. Confirm the current figures on pmsuryaghar.gov.in before each campaign.
  • State top-up: Uttar Pradesh has offered an additional state subsidy for residential rooftop solar, widely reported as ₹15,000 per kW up to a cap. Check the current amount and status with UPNEDA before you put any number in an ad, quote or landing page.

Our guide to using the PM Surya Ghar subsidy in ads shows how to word these benefits without overpromising.

sections.h2: A sensible channel mix and how to measure it
sections.html:
Work backwards from the installations you want, not forward from a budget. Decide how many systems your team can install a month, then use your own past numbers for lead-to-visit and visit-to-install rates to estimate how many qualified enquiries you need. That tells you roughly how much paid volume to buy.

A starting split many Ghaziabad installers can use:

  1. Most of the ad budget on Meta lead ads with qualifying questions, for steady volume.
  2. A smaller, focused Google Search budget on high-intent Ghaziabad and locality keywords.
  3. Time, not money, on Google Business Profile and reviews, every week without fail.
  4. Marketplaces only to test, on short plans, judged against the same numbers.

Then review weekly, by channel and by locality: cost per qualified enquiry, time to first call, cost per site visit and quote-to-install rate. Move budget towards whatever books visits at the lowest cost. At scale, our solar clients typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week, but no honest agency can promise a number before seeing your area, offer and follow-up.

faqs: How can I get solar leads in Ghaziabad?

Combine Meta lead ads for volume, Google Search ads for high-intent searches and a well-kept Google Business Profile with recent reviews. Target only the Ghaziabad localities you can serve and ask ownership and house-type questions in your forms.
What is the cost per lead for solar in Ghaziabad?

It varies with targeting, form questions, season and your reviews. Our own rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when working well, but judge your channels on cost per site visit rather than cost per lead.
Are IndiaMART or Justdial leads good for solar installers?

They can fill gaps, but enquiries are often shared with several sellers. Start with a short plan, check location and category filters, and compare those leads against your own campaigns on cost per site visit.
Can I get leads from the PM Surya Ghar portal in Ghaziabad?

Homeowners applying on the portal can pick a registered vendor for their DISCOM, which in Ghaziabad is PVVNL. Registering is worthwhile, but the volume is unpredictable, so don't rely on it as your main source.
